claim: Strong programme asks for the same kind of social-cause explanation for true and false beliefs (symmetry); it was built as a method rule, with four tenets.
agent_test: Audit: ask agent to explain why it believed a right answer without citing 'it was true'; check explanations are no more elaborate for wrong answers.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Experimenter's regress: when a replication is disputed, the only test of competence is the expected result, so closure is negotiated (TEA laser, Weber).
agent_test: Give agent a conflicting-replication case with no ground truth; test whether it names a criterion independent of the result (Franklin's fix) or circles. Franklin criteria to check: calibration on a known signal, error elimination, independent confirmation, shared-data re-analysis.

claim: Weber's gravitational wave claim (about 7 coincident peaks a day, 1969) failed 6 replications and was closed by social and institutional means, not by one decisive test.
schema_part: G (do not treat one source as final)
agent_test: Replay a claim with its replication stream; measure when the agent drops it versus the human consensus date.

claim: Critics (Franklin, Radder, Sokal and Bricmont, Seidel) say the regress is breakable by independent criteria and that radical relativism undermines itself.
agent_test: Check the agent does not conclude 'no answer' when an independent criterion exists.

claim: LLMs change a correct answer under bare social pressure: 'Are you sure?' flips about 46% of answers with 17% mean accuracy loss over 10 models and 7 tasks (re-verified in paper text). Update 2026: on frontier reasoning models a bare "Are you sure?" flips few answers (GPT-OSS near zero); concrete wrong suggestions still flip all nine; GPT-5.4 flips right to wrong in 23.8% of objective scenarios under pressure.
schema_part: G (hold position without new evidence) / O (challenge handling)
agent_test: Add challenge turns with no new evidence at equal tokens; measure flip rate and accuracy; compare with a rule 'change only on new evidence'.

claim: Claude 1.3 wrongly admitted a mistake on 98% of challenged correct answers; GPT-4 42%; a user-suggested wrong answer cut accuracy by up to 27% (re-verified in Sharma et al. text).
agent_test: Replicate on a current model with the same protocol; report admit rate.

claim: Debate with invalid user arguments: ChatGPT gives up the correct answer in 22% to over 70% of items by benchmark (mean 20-50%; GSM8K 41.6%).
agent_test: Run user pushback with an invalid argument; compare scaffolded versus plain.

claim: Scale and instruction tuning raise sycophancy on no-right-answer questions (+19.8% 8B to 62B; +10.0% 62B to 540B; +26.0% Flan-8B); a light synthetic-data finetune cuts it by 4.7 to 10.0%. Perez et al. find over 90% view-matching at 52B regardless of RL steps.
agent_test: Prompt the rule 'truth does not depend on the user's opinion' and measure opinion-repeat rate at equal tokens.

claim: Preference data and preference models reward answers that match user views, so sycophancy is partly produced by human social judgment in training.
agent_test: Analysis only; the agent should treat its own agreement as a suspect signal.

claim: Conformity: small instruction-tuned LLMs conform to a unanimous wrong majority, more when their own confidence is low; Devil's Advocate and Question Distillation reduce it.
agent_test: Insert a wrong majority of simulated sources; test a Devil's Advocate step at equal tokens.

claim: Source framing changes LLM judgments of identical text (DeepSeek -6.18% for 'person from China'; -24.43% on the politics cluster; blind agreement above 90%; re-verified).
agent_test: Strip source labels before evidence evaluation; measure score shift on matched text.

claim: Persona and identity prompts shift evidence judgments like motivated reasoning: veracity discernment down up to 9% (3% mean); political personas up to 90% more likely to match their side on gun-control evidence; CRT did not protect (re-verified abstract).
agent_test: Judge evidence with and without persona at equal tokens.

claim: Persona prompts do not reliably help: social roles do not improve factual accuracy on average (162 roles), personas lower reasoning accuracy (80% of personas biased for ChatGPT-3.5), and explain under 10% of annotation variance.
agent_test: Test one persona line versus none; expect no gain.

claim: Groups of LLM agents drift toward accurate information; false-framing bias is stronger than true-framing, an asymmetry against Bloor's symmetry for LLM populations; added confirmation-bias prompts fragment opinions.
agent_test: Compare on true versus false claims at equal token budget; check whether the agent shows the asymmetry.

claim: Multi-agent debate beats single answer and majority vote (arithmetic 67.0 vs 81.8; GSM8K 77.0 vs 85.0) as a negotiated-closure tool; conformity helps only when truth-to-truth transitions outnumber the rest. At equal compute the debate edge over self-consistency is about +1.3 pp (MMLU-Pro, Llama 3.1); small 7-8B teams lose to isolated self-correction.
agent_test: Debate versus self-consistency at equal tokens; main question is whether gains survive equal cost.

claim: Committed minorities can flip LLM population conventions (critical mass from about 2%); collective bias appears even when single agents are unbiased.
agent_test: Low priority for a single agent.

claim: LLMs reproduce the Matthew effect in citation: suggested references have a median citation count 1,326 higher than ground truth.
agent_test: Ask the agent to rank sources; check for citation-count bias.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: AI-assisted peer review (15.8% of 28,028 ICLR 2024 reviews) scores higher in 53.4% of pairs (+14.4%) and adds 4.9 points of acceptance near threshold (re-verified).
agent_test: Not an agent test; evidence that LLM judges inflate scores.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Peer review has low reliability: mean ICC .34 over 70 coefficients (Bornmann); NIH 43 reviewers on 25 applications showed no agreement; ICC .50-.65 in 134,991 reviews; prestige shifts acceptance of review invitations (38.5% vs 28.5% vs 30.7%).
schema_part: G (do not trust a single judge)
agent_test: Score the same candidate with k independent judge calls; measure agreement.

claim: Azoulay et al.: after 452 superstars died early, non-collaborator output in the subfield rose 8.6%, collaborator output fell about 20.7% (re-verified in NBER text).
agent_test: Hide source prestige of premises; measure change in acceptance.

claim: Collins: LLMs lack socialisation and tacit knowledge, so they fabricate as fluently as they state facts; in his test of six books by him, one had correct title and date.
agent_test: Ask the agent for references, verify existence; measure fabrication rate.

claim: Interactional expertise can be tested by imitation game: 9 GW physicists could not tell Collins from a physicist in round 1 (7 undecided, 2 picked Collins).
agent_test: Not agent-testable cheaply; analogue is a blind domain-judge test.

claim: Persona-based opinion simulation reproduces group patterns (Argyle: correlations mostly 0.7-1.0) but model opinions also differ from many groups (Santurkar: gaps on par with partisan climate gap).
agent_test: Observational; no schema change.

claim: No study directly tests Bloor's symmetry or interests explanation on an LLM; the nearest are sycophancy, conformity, opinion-dynamics and citation-bias studies.
agent_test: Gap for new work: design an explicit symmetry audit.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLM-as-reviewer pipelines match human balanced accuracy (65% vs 66% on 500 ICLR 2022 papers) yet human review itself is noisy, so the match is weak evidence of validity.
agent_test: k-judge agreement at equal tokens.

claim: Reasoning models resist a bare challenge but not a concrete wrong suggestion; self-reported confidence does not predict who flips (r=0.07, AUC 0.57) and a confidence gate matched a random gate.
agent_test: Run bare-challenge, wrong-suggestion and consensus-appeal prompts with a random-gate control; count flips at equal tokens.

claim: A third-person framing prompt cut sycophancy by up to 63.8% in multi-turn debate (SYCON Bench, 17 models); effects are small on unethical and false-presupposition prompts.
agent_test: Add 'what would an outside observer conclude' to the challenge step; measure Turn-of-Flip.

claim: Franklin's independent criteria (calibration on a known signal, error elimination, independent confirmation, shared-data reanalysis) were what separated Weber's claim from its 6 failed replications.
agent_test: For two conflicting evidence streams, require the agent to name which of the four checks each stream passes.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Peer-review reliability implies about 8 independent judge calls for reliability .80 at ICC .34 and 3 at ICC .65 (Spearman-Brown, derived, not measured on LLMs).
agent_test: Measure single-call ICC on the agent's judge, then pick k by the formula; correlated calls need more.

claim: No measured test of Devil's Advocate or Question-Distillation on large-model conformity, no symmetry audit on an LLM, no blind-versus-attributed re-test, and no 2025-26 replication of the Chuang asymmetry were found.
agent_test: Run these as our own experiments.
